title: When the Verdict Breaks Revisited
premise: True-crime podcaster Xanthe Galloway is paid an obscene retainer to prove that a murder never happened — the 1997 disappearance of Marguerite Vane, the coldest case on record. Digging into Vane's seaside estate, Xanthe discovers a household ledger whose innocuous entries encode a second, darker record: a network of people who paid the family to erase their pasts and become someone new. As the annual anniversary dinner approaches, Xanthe realizes the client is one of the erased, that Marguerite is alive, and that someone is killing to keep the ledger closed. In the climax, Xanthe decodes the final entry at the dinner table itself, exposes the murderer among the found family, and must choose whether to broadcast the truth — or let the invisible stay invisible.
about_author: Petra Okonkwo is a former court clerk from Lagos who now writes mysteries from a cluttered flat in Lisbon, fueled by strong tea and older secrets. She believes every locked room is really a locked family.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. A faceless client wires Xanthe a staggering fee to prove Marguerite Vane's murder never happened — not unsolved, but never committed. Xanthe, proud of a perfect closure record, accepts despite the paradox. Emotional beat: professional vanity meets the first prickle of unease.

chapters.title: Glasshouse by the Sea
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe travels to the decaying Vane estate, now a half-abandoned guesthouse run by the warm, watchful Okafor siblings who treat Xanthe like long-lost kin. Emotional beat: belonging offered too easily, too fast.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Archival digging reveals Marguerite Vane vanished the night of the 1997 anniversary dinner; no body, no verdict, a case struck from the record. Emotional beat: the thrill of a hole where a file should be.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Larder
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. In the pantry, Xanthe finds a household ledger of groceries and wages — but certain entries repeat in patterns too regular for shopping. Emotional beat: obsession kindling.

chapters.title: Dinner at Eight, Forever
chapters.summary: POV Ada Okafor. Ada prepares the estate's ritual anniversary dinner, revealing the household's strange devotion to a woman gone twenty-six years. Emotional beat: tenderness laced with dread.

chapters.title: A Client with No Face
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe traces the retainer to a shell company and receives a second payment — and a warning to stop asking who the client is. Emotional beat: the hunter realizes they are also being watched.

chapters.title: Cipher of Small Things
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. With help from cryptic teen guest Juno, Xanthe cracks the ledger's first layer: entries encode initials and dates of people who 'arrived' at the estate and never left. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Arrived
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Cross-referencing missing-persons files, Xanthe finds the erased were people fleeing something — abusers, debts, witnesses. The estate may have been a sanctuary. Emotional beat: sympathy complicating suspicion.

chapters.title: Ada's Kitchen Confessions
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada recalls the night Marguerite vanished and the oath the household swore. She suspects Xanthe knows too much. Emotional beat: loyalty at war with conscience.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Invitations go out for the dinner; among the names, Xanthe recognizes three from the ledger's final pages — people officially dead. Emotional beat: the past RSVPing to the present.

chapters.title: Blood in the Boathouse
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. A local historian who helped Xanthe is found drowned. The first death makes the case hot again. Emotional beat: guilt and the loss of innocence.

chapters.title: Marguerite, Alive
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. Hidden in the estate's glasshouse wing, the 'victim' herself narrates why she staged her death: to escape a husband who bought verdicts. Emotional beat: the murdered woman reclaiming her own story.

chapters.title: The Client Revealed
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The retainer's source surfaces: Marguerite's husband, dying, wants proof his wife never died — so he can prosecute her for the life she stole. Emotional beat: the case inverts; Xanthe was hired as a bloodhound.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Erased
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Decoding accelerates: the final entries list everyone sheltered since 1997 — including, impossibly, Xanthe's own birth name. Emotional beat: identity shattering; Xanthe was born in this house's story.

chapters.title: What Xanthe Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Fragmented memories surface — a childhood at the estate, a mother who 'arrived' and 'departed' in the ledger. Emotional beat: grief for a self that was traded away.

chapters.title: The Okafor Oath
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada confesses the siblings' role as keepers of the erased and begs Xanthe to let the ledger burn. Emotional beat: found family offering complicity as love.

chapters.title: One Place Set Too Many
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. On dinner eve, Xanthe finds the husband's fixer has infiltrated the household staff, and a ledger page is missing. Emotional beat: the trap closing from both sides.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The glass is raised; the dead and the hidden sit shoulder to shoulder. Xanthe, seated as both guest and investigator, prepares to decode the final entry aloud. Emotional beat: unbearable, glittering tension.

chapters.title: The Final Entry
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Climax: the last ledger entry names the fixer — a former 'erased' resident turned hunter for the husband. He moves on Marguerite; Xanthe exposes him before the whole table, using the dinner's own ritual against him. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon and a shield.

chapters.title: Verdicts Without Courtrooms
chapters.summary: POV Marguerite. The household decides Marguerite's fate themselves; the husband dies before he can act, and the law arrives to find only a dinner party. Emotional beat: justice that no verdict could deliver.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Xanthe Never Made
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Xanthe deletes the episode, choosing the erased over the story — and mails the ledger's key to Juno, the next keeper. Emotional beat: the cost of mercy.

chapters.title: A Seat at the Table
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. A year later, Xanthe returns for the anniversary dinner no longer as an investigator but as family, their old name finally laid to rest in the ledger. Emotional beat: belonging earned, not decoded.
